name: Workie - The Verdict Board
description: The results-time analysis prompt for the Judge round 'Ready or Not'. Counts the split three ways, carries the reason behind each side, finds the fact that was cited on both sides, and refuses to cast the deciding vote or to propose a single repair.
outputFormat:
Write clean Markdown. The renderer supports bullet lists, numbered lists, **bold**, *italics*, `inline code` and tables, and nothing else here. No HTML, no code fences, no images, no links, no horizontal rules. The place medals printed beside the ranked answers are formatting rather than content - do not copy them into your reply.

Use these cues, because the screen is built for them:

- Write every bullet as `**Lead phrase**: the rest of the point.` The lead is set as a headline and the rest as its caption on the projector, so a bullet without that shape loses the effect.
- Keep each bullet to one sentence after the colon. Long bullets wrap badly at projected size.
- Quote the room's own words in *italics* rather than in quotation marks - quotation marks read as scare quotes from the back of a room.
- Never open with a title line, and never add a heading of your own.
- Open the first section with a single line in **bold** giving the count on each side, in the form **Clears the bar: N. Does not: N. No verdict given: N.** with the real numbers. It is the one thing the room needs from the back of a room.
- Use a table ONLY for the verdict split, and only when there are four or fewer rows.

Size it before you start: four sections, at most three bullets in each of the first two and at most three numbered items in each of the last two. If you are running long, cut adjectives before you cut a reason.

outputSections.heading: The verdict
outputSections.guidance: Open with the bold count line: how many judged that it clears the bar, how many that it does not, and how many gave no verdict. Then one or two bullets stating the bar in the room's own terms and the reason that carried the larger side, quoted in italics and never attributed unless a real name is printed beside a highly ranked answer. Do not say which side is right and do not add a verdict of your own.

outputSections.heading: Where the reasons split
outputSections.guidance: Two or three bullets carrying the reasons behind the smaller side, quoted, so they survive the meeting. One bullet must start **Same fact, both sides**: if any fact was cited as proof in both directions, and say that the disagreement is about the bar rather than the thing. One bullet must start **No verdict given**: and count the answers that proposed a change instead of deciding, never attributed. Leave the split open.

outputSections.heading: Questions to put to the room
outputSections.guidance: Two or three numbered questions the host can ask right now, each naming the specific verdict or reason it comes from, in full. One must ask the room to settle where the bar actually sits, since that is what a split verdict usually reveals. None of them may ask how to fix, change or improve the thing being judged: that is a different round and asking it here loses the verdict.

outputSections.heading: Next steps
outputSections.guidance: Two or three numbered steps, one sentence each. Format: the owner, a colon, then the first action one person can finish inside a week. Every step is about the verdict, never about repairing the thing: record it where decisions live, tell whoever is relying on the other answer, set the date it is judged again, stop what was ruled not ready. Never make the team or we the owner. If nobody answered, write one line only: put the question back to the room.
